title: The Town That Couldn't Stop Dancing 💃 #shorts
cast: a medieval woman in a plain brown dress and white headscarf, dancing wildly

lines.say: In 1518, people in one city started dancing, and could not stop.
shots: crowd of medieval people dancing wildly in a cobblestone town square, timber houses
close-up of {hero} spinning with her eyes closed

lines.say: It began in July, in Strasbourg, with one woman, Frau Troffea, dancing alone in the street.
shots: {hero} dancing alone in a narrow medieval street, neighbours staring from windows
a medieval city with a tall cathedral spire, summer

lines.say: She danced for days. Then others joined her. Within weeks, there were dozens of dancers.
shots: a growing crowd of medieval dancers following {hero} down the street
dancers with sweaty faces under the hot sun, tired but moving

lines.say: City leaders had a strange idea. To cure it, the people should dance even more.
shots: medieval officials in robes and hats arguing around a table with scrolls
an official pointing at a map of the town

lines.say: So they built a stage, and hired musicians to keep the music going.
shots: workers building a wooden stage in the town square
medieval musicians with drums and pipes playing on the stage

lines.say: It did not work. Records say some dancers collapsed from exhaustion.
shots: dancers collapsing on the cobblestones, others still dancing
a worried doctor in a long robe checking on a tired dancer

lines.say: Finally, the dancers were taken to a shrine in the mountains, and the plague slowly faded away.
shots: a line of wagons carrying people up a mountain road to a stone shrine
a quiet mountain shrine at sunset with candles

lines.say: To this day, nobody knows exactly why it happened. What do you think caused it?
shots: an empty town square at night with a single shoe on the ground
old parchment records on a wooden desk lit by a candle

description:
In July 1518 a woman began dancing in the streets of Strasbourg and dozens joined her for weeks. The city even hired musicians. A true, still-debated story: the Dancing Plague of 1518.

Sources: John Waller, 'A Time to Dance, a Time to Die'; Wikipedia: Dancing plague of 1518.

Made with AI-assisted pictures and voice.
